alex: hey — console is collapsing the x-request-id column for some requests (shows ...abcd). I only have the truncated tail (abcd). How can I reliably find the full request logs? :mag_right:
priya: hey alex :wave: if console truncates it you can still search via the request trace id or by correlating timestamps. quick options: redwoodctl (our CLI) or grep the edge proxy logs.
priya: redwoodctl example (run from devbox with creds):
```
redwoodctl logs --request-id "abcd" --fuzzy
# or use full match if you have more chars: redwoodctl logs --request-id "...abcd" --since 10m
```
priya: the --fuzzy flag tries prefix/suffix matches across stored request refs. It hits the log index and span links.
dan: if you don't have redwoodctl handy, try searching the edge proxy (nginx/katran) for the header name we inject: X-RW-REQ. on the cluster: 
```
kubectl -n edge logs -l app=edge-proxy --since=15m | rg "abcd" -n
```
dan: also look for the trace id in the span link printed in the console trace column (if present) and use otel-lookup: 
```
otel-lookup trace 1a2b3c4d5e --from 2024-05-01T12:00:00Z
```
alex: otel-lookup isn't in my PATH. can you share a more concrete step for the trace -> log line mapping? I'm seeing span ids but not sure where to paste them. :thinking_face:
priya: sure — if you have a trace id (e.g., 1a2b3c4d5e) you can get the spans and look for attributes x.request_id / http.request.header.x-rw-req. then grep logs with that full header. quick flow: 
1) in console click span -> copy trace id
2) run: otel-lookup trace <trace-id> --format json | jq -r '.spans[] | select(.attributes["http.request.header.x-rw-req"]) | .attributes["http.request.header.x-rw-req"]'
3) take that header value and run kubectl or redwoodctl logs with it
priya: if you can't run jq, paste the trace id here and I can pull it for you (have cluster access).
infra-bot: hint: we also index request_id into the ELK cluster under field request.identifier — Kibana quick link: https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#/?_a=(query:(match:(request.identifier:(query:abcd))))
alex: thanks — I was missing the header name mapping. one follow-up: any perf impact from running redwoodctl --fuzzy across many days? wondering if we should be careful on prod peak.
jack: good q. non-admin fuzzy searches are rate-limited. for heavy hunts use a time-bound query ( --since / --until ) or ask infra to run a backfilled search. we also have a dataplane job that can do a deep index scan during off-peak.
dan: FYI if console truncation is frequent we should surface full request ids in the trace popup — opened a tiny RFC: https://go.redwood/wip/obs-trace-popup (short-term we can add copy-to-clipboard for the full header).
alex: awesome, i'll try redwoodctl + otel-lookup with the full header flow. will paste results if I hit a wall. thanks all :thumbsup:
priya: ping me if you want me to run the trace query for you. happy to help.
